<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19143>

Ivan Krylov (<mailto:ikrylov@disroot.org|ikrylov@disroot.org>) changed:

           What    |Removed                     |Added
----------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- Comment #1 from Ivan Krylov (<mailto:ikrylov@disroot.org|ikrylov@disroot.org>) ---
Could you please share your `sessionInfo()`? My Windows machines seem to
preserve the locale name I give them.

What is the underlying issue here? What is broken by having a UTF-8 string
being marked as `CE_NATIVE` when the native encoding is UTF-8? R is full of
such strings. `charIsUTF8()` is true for them. Both `translateChar()` and
`translateCharUTF8()` return the underlying buffer.

Meanwhile, even latest R can still run on legacy Windows systems with an 8-bit
codepage instead of UTF-8, where the non-ASCII encoding name must be marked as
`CE_NATIVE`:

```
> Sys.setlocale("LC_TIME", "Norwegian Bokmål_Norway") |> tools::showNonASCII()
1: Norwegian Bokm<e5>l_Norway.1252
> sessionInfo()
R Under development (unstable) (2026-07-19 r90279 ucrt)
Platform: x86_64-w64-mingw32/x64
Running under: Windows Server 2022 x64 (build 20348)

Matrix products: default
  LAPACK version 3.12.1

locale:
[1] LC_COLLATE=English_United States.1252 
[2] LC_CTYPE=English_United States.1252   
[3] LC_MONETARY=English_United States.1252
[4] LC_NUMERIC=C                          
[5] LC_TIME=Norwegian Bokmål_Norway.1252  

time zone: Europe/Moscow
tzcode source: internal

attached base packages:
[1] stats     graphics  grDevices utils     datasets  methods   base     

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
[1] compiler_4.7.0 tools_4.7.0   
```

What needs to be fixed for non-ASCII locale names to work is
`CHAR(STRING_ELT(locale, 0))` (it must be `translateChar(STRING_ELT(locale,
0))`, subject to the chicken-and-egg problem of what's valid in the current
encoding); otherwise non-ASCII locale names won't work unless the string
contents happen to coincide with the ANSI/UTF-8 encoding expected by the CRT.

        #define p(x) printf("%s => %s\n", #x, x)
        p(setlocale(LC_ALL, ""));

        p(setlocale(LC_CTYPE, "C"));
        p(setlocale(LC_CTYPE, bokmaal_utf8));
        p(setlocale(LC_CTYPE, bokmaal_latin1));
}

--- Comment #4 from Kevin Ushey (<mailto:kevinushey@gmail.com|kevinushey@gmail.com>) ---
Hmm...

```
> l <- 'Norwegian Bokmål_Norway.utf8'
> 
> Encoding(l)
[1] "UTF-8"
> Sys.setlocale('LC_CTYPE', l)
[1] "Norwegian Bokmål_Norway.utf8"
> Sys.setlocale('LC_CTYPE', 'C')
[1] "C"
> enc2native(l)
[1] "Norwegian Bokm<U+00E5>l_Norway.utf8"
> Sys.setlocale('LC_CTYPE', l)
Warning in Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", l) :
  OS reports request to set locale to "Norwegian BokmÃ¥l_Norway.utf8" cannot be
honored
[1] ""
> 
> l <- 'Norwegian Bokmål_Norway.utf8'
> 
> Encoding(l)
[1] "unknown"
> Sys.setlocale('LC_CTYPE', l)
[1] "Norwegian Bokmål_Norway.utf8"
> Sys.setlocale('LC_CTYPE', 'C')
[1] "C"
> enc2native(l)
[1] "Norwegian Bokm\345l_Norway.utf8"
> Sys.setlocale('LC_CTYPE', l)
[1] "Norwegian Bokmål_Norway.utf8"
```

But at the heart of this, R extracts the requested locale (in do_setlocale)
with:

        const char *l = CHAR(STRING_ELT(locale, 0));

and IIUC that will do the wrong thing if the locale itself isn't in the
(current) native encoding. I guess there are two ways forward: translate that
locale to the native encoding before use, or use the "wide" APIs for setting
and getting the locale on Windows.

(UCRT assigning meaning to bytes outside ASCII in the `C` locale).
